prompt.content:
You are a power system operator solving a DC optimal power flow problem.

Network: 7 buses (bus 0 is the slack/reference bus).

Transmission lines (DC power flow; bus angles theta in radians; the MW flow on a line from bus i to bus j is: flow_MW = 100 * (theta_i - theta_j) / reactance_pu, i.e. per-unit flow on a 100 MVA base converted to MW; the limit applies to |flow_MW| in both directions):
  Line 0: bus 0 <-> bus 1, reactance 0.2208 p.u., flow limit 134.6 MW
  Line 1: bus 0 <-> bus 3, reactance 0.0537 p.u., flow limit 153.0 MW
  Line 2: bus 0 <-> bus 4, reactance 0.2354 p.u., flow limit 166.3 MW
  Line 3: bus 0 <-> bus 6, reactance 0.2231 p.u., flow limit 154.5 MW
  Line 4: bus 1 <-> bus 5, reactance 0.0628 p.u., flow limit 41.6 MW
  Line 5: bus 2 <-> bus 3, reactance 0.1355 p.u., flow limit 44.9 MW
  Line 6: bus 2 <-> bus 6, reactance 0.2476 p.u., flow limit 121.0 MW
  Line 7: bus 3 <-> bus 4, reactance 0.1596 p.u., flow limit 137.5 MW
  Line 8: bus 3 <-> bus 5, reactance 0.1806 p.u., flow limit 163.5 MW

Generators:
  Gen 0: at bus 4, cost $29.7/MWh, output range [8.9, 86.0] MW
  Gen 1: at bus 0, cost $52.81/MWh, output range [5.0, 85.5] MW
  Gen 2: at bus 3, cost $55.66/MWh, output range [7.9, 144.1] MW

Loads:
  Bus 0: 22.7 MW
  Bus 2: 30.8 MW
  Bus 3: 46.2 MW
  Bus 4: 73.4 MW

Find the generator dispatch that minimizes total cost ($/h) while:
1. Total generation equals total load (173.1 MW)
2. Each generator stays within its output range
3. No line flow exceeds its MW limit (DC power flow physics with the given reactances)

Report each MW value to at least one decimal place. Constraints are verified
with a +/-0.5 MW tolerance, but imbalance or bound violations inside that
tolerance are penalized in the cost scoring, so target exact feasibility.

Respond with your final answer as JSON on the last line, exactly in this format:
{"dispatch_mw": [<Gen 0 MW>, <Gen 1 MW>, ...]}
